title: SRE operator journal — API degradation patterns and response checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working operator journal for common HTTP/API degradation modes we see in the inference stack: server-side timeouts, 429s (rate limiting/backpressure), degraded streaming (chunked responses stalling or truncating), and bursts of elevated 5xx/4xx error rates.

Scope & intent:
- Quick-reference heuristics for first responders (on-call SRE/engineer)
- Lightweight checklist to get service to stable state and minimize customer impact
- Capture of recurring root-cause patterns and mitigation experiments to try later
- NOT a replacement for formal post-incident writeups — this should feed those.

High-level symptoms to distinguish quickly:
- Global latency spike across models/routes + increased queued requests -> likely autoscale / backend saturation or queueing (GPU hot nodes).
- Sudden rise in 429s with low latency on responses -> likely token-bucket rate limiter triggered (edge or gateway).
- Streaming sessions open for long time with little data -> KV cache miss storms, blob store or network egress problem, or chunking layer failure.
- Rising 50x errors correlated with model variant rollouts -> bad model artifact or runtime regression.

Fast triage (first 5–10 minutes):
1) Pager info & scope: which route/service/component? Grab pager alert text and link to the incident channel.
2) Surface metrics: open Grafana dashboard: "API - latency & errors (prod)" and "Serving - queue depth & GPU utilization". Look at p50/p95/p99 and error rate by route.
3) Evidence collection (do this while talking to channel):
   - PromQL quick checks (copy/paste):
     * increase(rate(http_server_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[1m]))
     * sum(rate(api_response_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route) -> quick latency histogram per route
     * sum(rate(api_throttled_total[1m])) by (route)
   - kubectl: kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/api-gateway; kubectl -n prod get pods -o wide | grep api-gateway
   - Check model-serving pool: k get pods -n serving -l app=model-server -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.phase}'
4) Customer impact triage: Which customers/routes are impacted? Pin high-traffic or enterprise routes first.

Common patterns, root-cause signals & quick mitigations:
A) Timeouts (upstream response timeouts)
Signals: p99 latency for model-server rising, gateway returns 504, GPU pods show high CPU/RAM or NVML GPU util > 90%, request queues growing. Logs show repeated retry loops.
Immediate mitigations:
- Activate fallback model route (lower-cost/smaller model) if configured: /route -> fallback_v1.
- Scale up serving pool (if Dedicated): kubectl scale deploy/model-server --replicas=N+2 or trigger autoscale policy; for hosted, trigger incident runbook to request burst capacity from infra.
- If warm cache helps: toggle prefix-cache-enabled=true on the routing config (note: causes short-term cold misses).
- If single node is hot: cordon/evict that pod and let HPA reschedule: kubectl drain pod/<pod> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data then monitor.
Notes: avoid immediate restarts of all pods; prefer targeted drain/replace.

B) 429s (rate-limit/backpressure)
Signals: client-visible 429s spike, gateway metrics show increase in throttled count, short latency for 429 responses, token-bucket occupancy at limit, linkerd/envoy downstream queue length small.
Quick mitigations:
- Identify which limiter triggered (edge vs internal). Query limiter metrics: rate(api_rate_limiter_rejections[1m]).
- Temporarily raise per-route token/burst allowance for critical customers: update limiter config for route X -> burst +20% (patch envoy config or feature flag).
- Throttle non-critical routes or bulk endpoints: enable shard-level denylist.
- If due to retry storms from clients: add short 200ms jittered retry-backoff header response for observed clients, or return Retry-After header.
- If caused by internal surge (batch job), find job and pause it. Check batch job run history: kubectl -n jobs get jobs | grep nightly-large-batch.
Notes: document raise in ops channel and revert after stabilization. Always note which config change and owner.

C) Degraded streaming (chunked responses stall, partial messages)
Signals: streaming sessions remain open, little bytes transferred, client-side sees stalled "event" chunks, server logs show broken pipe or keepalive timeouts, network egress errors to CDN or proxy.
Quick mitigations:
- Toggle streaming -> polling fallback: set header X-Fallback-To-Polling: true for critical clients (configurable in gateway).
- Restart gateway streaming workers if only gateway shows errors (targeted restart).
- Check the TCP connection count and ephemeral port exhaustion on gateway nodes: netstat metrics. If port exhaustion, roll nodes behind load balancer.
- If blob store or message broker is slow (we use NATS/kafka for stream chunks), check broker lag and restart brokers if needed.
Notes: prefer graceful restarts and draining to avoid cutting open streams; inform clients about degraded mode.

D) Elevated error rates (5xx bursts)
Signals: spike in 5xx across many routes; often follows deploy, config change, or external dependency failure (auth, db).
Quick mitigations:
- Rollback last deploy immediately if deploy timestamp correlates (kubectl rollout undo).
- If auth failures, check KMS / token service health; rotate to backup auth endpoint if available.
- Enable automatic fallback policy: route requests to stable model/version for routes with >X% errors (feature flag).
- If errors are noisy but isolated to one region, trigger cross-region failover routing.

Observability checklist (what to open immediately):
- API Gateways: request rate, 429s, 5xxs by route, p99 latency, connection count
- Serving pool: GPU utiliz, queue length per pod, OOMs, crashloop logs
- Autoscaler: current replicas, HPA metrics, pending pods due to quota or scheduling failure
- Edge infra: load balancer health, network errors, iptables drops, ephemeral port exhaustion
- Downstream deps: cache hit ratio, DB error rates, auth service latency
- Logs: search for stack traces, OOM, ENOMEM, disk full, 'no such file or directory' on model artifact loads

Run commands & useful one-liners (operator cheat sheet):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-gateway -o wide
- kubectl logs -n serving <pod> -c model-server --since=10m | tail -n 200
- kubectl exec -n infra <pod> -- netstat -anp | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l (port exhaustion check)
- PromQL: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m])) by (status, route)
- Grafana panels to open: API - error heatmap, Serving - memory & GPU, Rate limiter dashboard, Stream throughput

Communication playbook (first 15–30 mins):
- Create incident channel #incident-api-<short-id> and post initial facts: when triggered, scope, customers impacted, immediate mitigations applied.
- Notify Customer Success for high-touch customers and provide ETA.
- Post update every 15 min until stable: what we observed, what we tried, next steps.
- If we have to change customer-facing behavior (fallbacks, degraded streaming), post template: what changed, why, how to opt out, rollback plan.

Post-incident follow-up (required fields for RCA):
- Timeline: alerts, mitigation actions, rollbacks, customer reports
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (metrics/logs/traces)
- Corrective actions: runbook updates, config changes, alert tuning, capacity changes, code fixes, tests to add (load tests / chaos experiments)
- Owners and deadlines for each corrective action

Known quirks / heuristics from past incidents (quick notes):
- Short-lived 429 spikes often coincide with KV cache warmup cycles after a deployment. Pattern: cache-miss storm -> backend saturation -> gateway throttles -> 429. Pre-warm caches on deploy to avoid.
- Streaming degrade + modest 5xxs often point to egress network saturation (egress bandwidth limit hit). Fix: increase NIC, or reduce per-stream throughput by switching to compressed chunks.
- Sudden p99 jumps with no 5xx: often noisy clients sending long-context prompts. Consider per-request token caps or prompt-length-based circuit breaker.

Experiment log (things we've tried):
- Auto-fallback to smaller model variant during CPU/GPU saturation: good for latency but increased hallucination risk; needs QA gating.
- Aggressive caching of initial prompt prefixes: reduced token cost by ~18% on average for chat workloads in prod test cluster.
- Jittered Retry-After header for clients with poor backoff: reduced retry storms, but some clients ignored header.

TODOs (short list):
- Formalize streaming -> polling fallback feature flag and test across top-5 customers (owner: Li Wei, due 2026-03-20).
- Add Grafana alert: sustained token-bucket rejections > 100/min for 3m per route (owner: Ravi).
- Implement canary pre-warm cache hook in deploy pipeline (owner: Sofia).
- Add automated consumer telemetry for client retry behavior (investigate adding header propagation).

Notes to self (things I noticed, unverified):
- Saw a pattern where one enterprise customer with aggressive retry backoff caused cluster-wide 429s during a model promotion. Need to identify their client id and onboard them to better retry rules.
- Consider a per-customer emergency bypass token for high-paying customers during incidents. Security review required.

End of draft. Keep this file lean and iterative — add short examples from future incidents, and prune older heuristics that no longer match the runtime.
